teachingPoint: The registers worked exactly as designed here: the object was listed, the claim was substantiated, and the case still took twelve years and a seizure to resolve. A high-coverage, high-confidence passport is a starting point for a legal process, not a substitute for one.
explanation:
PROVENANCE CONFIDENCE SCORE: 28/100
The score is built by accumulation, not by deduction. It starts at 30 (the honest baseline for 'nothing is known') and gains credit for authoritative records (+18 each) and press reports (+8 each). Gaps in the early chain, and hits in stolen-art registers, subtract points. An object with no published history scores near 30 — not near 100. Absence of evidence is not evidence of clean provenance.

Score build-up:
  +30 — base score — 'nothing is known' starting position (ADR-002) → running total: 30
  +18 — authority record: "Egon Schiele painted 'Portrait of Wally' (Bildnis Wally) in 1912, depicting his model and companion Walburga Neuzil. Oil on wood panel, 32 × 39.8 cm (portrait orientation). The painting was one of Schiele's most personal works, completed during the height of his Expressionist period." → running total: 48
  +18 — authority record: "Acquired by Lea Bondi Jaray, a prominent Viennese art dealer, at an unknown date before 1925. Bondi Jaray was the sole proprietor of the Würthle Gallery, Vienna, and one of the early significant collectors of Schiele's work." → running total: 66
  +18 — authority record: "Following the Anschluss (annexation of Austria, March 1938) and under direct duress from Friedrich Welz, a Nazi-affiliated art dealer who had been appointed commissioner for Aryanisation of Viennese art galleries, Lea Bondi Jaray was forced to transfer 'Portrait of Wally' to Welz. Bondi Jaray received no payment and immediately fled Austria for London. This transfer is the subject of the Lost Art Foundation registration." → running total: 84
  +18 — authority record: "US Second Circuit Court of Appeals ruled (2001) that 'Portrait of Wally' constituted stolen property under the National Stolen Property Act (NSPA) and that the case could proceed to trial. This was a landmark ruling on the application of the NSPA to Nazi-looted art." → running total: 102
  +18 — authority record: "The painting is registered in the Lost Art Database (Kulturgutverluste.de) as a case of Nazi-era cultural property spoliation. The registration reflects the 1938 forced transfer from Lea Bondi Jaray and the subsequent restitution-by-settlement in 2010. The case is a primary reference in European and US Holocaust-era art restitution law." → running total: 120
  +8 — press report: "After World War II (c. 1945–1954) the painting passed through Austrian state custody. It was eventually acquired by Rudolf Leopold, a Viennese ophthalmologist and collector, who built what became the Leopold Collection. Leopold acquired the painting in the 1950s, reportedly without knowledge of the forced transfer from Bondi Jaray. The 1945–1954 ownership gap is genuine and was acknowledged in the subsequent litigation." → running total: 128
  +8 — press report: "The painting was included in a major Egon Schiele exhibition on loan from the Leopold Collection at the Museum of Modern Art, New York (5 October 1997). Heirs of Lea Bondi Jaray filed a request with the Manhattan DA for the painting to be held pending investigation of Nazi-era provenance. The Manhattan DA issued a subpoena; the painting was seized by New York authorities and held at the MoMA for years." → running total: 136
  +8 — press report: "Settlement reached: the Leopold Museum (which had absorbed the Leopold Collection) agreed to pay $19 million to the heirs of Lea Bondi Jaray in exchange for the release of the painting. The settlement, announced July 2010, allowed the Leopold Museum to retain the painting while acknowledging the Nazi-era provenance claim. 'Portrait of Wally' is now permanently displayed at the Leopold Museum, Vienna." → running total: 144
  -44 — cap at 100 (positive-evidence ceiling) → running total: 100
  -12 — provenance gap (0 undated event(s); no complete chain before earliest record) → running total: 88
  -20 — register hit: "INTERPOL cultural heritage materials reference Schiele's Portrait of Wally as a canonical Nazi-era spoliation case" → running total: 68
  -20 — register hit: "FBI Art Crime Team has documented Schiele's Portrait of Wally as a major Nazi-era art restitution case; painting was seized in New York (1997) under National Stolen Property Act" → running total: 48
  -20 — register hit: "Lost Art Database: Egon Schiele, Portrait of Wally (1912) — registered as Nazi-era spoliation; forced transfer from Lea Bondi Jaray to Friedrich Welz, Vienna 1938" → running total: 28

EVIDENCE COVERAGE: WELL-COVERED
3 of 9 registers could systematically name this object. Silence here is comparatively informative: records would be expected to exist.
Registers that could have systematically named this object: Lost Art Database, Getty Provenance Index, Art Loss Register. A quiet result from these registers is meaningful — records would be expected to exist.
Registers applicable but not identifying (category-level or attention-driven): Wikidata. Silence from these carries little evidential weight.
5 register(s) cannot structurally hold an object of this type or origin. Their silence says nothing.

WHAT THIS SCORE DOES NOT MEAN:
A high score is not a declaration of clean provenance. It means sourced evidence was found — not that the evidence is complete, not that no problem exists outside what was checked, and not that the object is legally safe to sell or exhibit.
A low score is not an accusation of looting. Under the accumulation model, a low score means evidence was not found — which may mean the documentary record is genuinely thin, or may mean the registers that could have spoken simply do not cover material of this type.
This score does not assess forgery risk. Whether the image is what it claims to be is a separate question on the same scale — see forgeryRisk.

COMPARABILITY:
This score is comparable only to other well covered objects. Comparison against a structurally uncovered object will understate how little was checked there.
The score is an ordinal measure within a coverage class, not a universal percentage. Ranking objects from different coverage classes by score is an analytical error equivalent to comparing temperatures in Celsius and Fahrenheit without converting.

RISK FLAGS (7):
  [HIGH] repatriationPrecedent: Timeline cites a repatriation/illicit-excavation event: "US Second Circuit Court of Appeals ruled (2001) that 'Portrait of Wally' constituted stolen property under the National Stolen Property Act (NSPA) and that the case could proceed to trial. This was a landmark ruling on the application of the NSPA to Nazi-looted art."
  [MEDIUM] lootingSignal: Object history intersects a documented looting/repatriation case.
  [MEDIUM] provenanceGap: Pre-acquisition history is incomplete (0 undated event(s); no documented chain before earliest record).
  [HIGH] registrySignal: Register source describes this object in theft/looting/restitution terms: "INTERPOL cultural heritage materials reference Schiele's Portrait of Wally as a canonical Nazi-era spoliation case". Verify against the register itself before relying on it.
  [HIGH] registrySignal: Register source describes this object in theft/looting/restitution terms: "FBI Art Crime Team has documented Schiele's Portrait of Wally as a major Nazi-era art restitution case; painting was seized in New York (1997) under National Stolen Property Act". Verify against the register itself before relying on it.
  [HIGH] registrySignal: Register source describes this object in theft/looting/restitution terms: "Lost Art Database: Egon Schiele, Portrait of Wally (1912) — registered as Nazi-era spoliation; forced transfer from Lea Bondi Jaray to Friedrich Welz, Vienna 1938". Verify against the register itself before relying on it.
  [LOW] registryCoverageGap: 2 of 9 registers have no public API and were not searched (INTERPOL SWOA, FBI NSAF, Carabinieri TPC among them). Their silence here means nothing — the official searches must be run by hand.

disclosure.public:
Role: Public
Description: Anyone. Sees that the object exists, its confidence score with its coverage class, and that it was notarised — and nothing that could identify or endanger the holder.

Fields visible:
  • public: object identity, title, artist, cultural context, image hash, confidence score, coverage class, and the notarisation proof

Fields withheld:
  • source-community: claim status, custodianship terms, and source-community statements
    Reason: Community-facing fields (claim status, custodianship) are tagged source-community and are not visible to ladder roles. They belong to the community, not the institution.
  • museum: physical dimensions, condition, loan eligibility, risk flags, and forensic scores
    Reason: Requires "museum" access level; this role is at "public" on the disclosure ladder.
  • enforcement: full provenance timeline, registry hits, current location, holder pseudonym, and contact escrow
    Reason: Requires "enforcement" access level; this role is at "public" on the disclosure ladder.
  • owner: holder identity and all fields above
    Reason: Requires "owner" access level; this role is at "public" on the disclosure ladder.
disclosure.source-community:
Role: Source community
Description: A community with an ancestral or territorial connection to the object. Sees the public tier plus claim status, custodianship terms and community statements. Never sees museum or enforcement internals.

Fields visible:
  • public: object identity, title, artist, cultural context, image hash, confidence score, coverage class, and the notarisation proof
  • source-community: claim status, custodianship terms, and source-community statements

Fields withheld:
  • museum: physical dimensions, condition, loan eligibility, risk flags, and forensic scores
    Reason: Source communities have a legitimate interest in cultural claim information but not in institutional or enforcement internals. The orthogonal role model prevents this role from seeing museum or enforcement data regardless of ladder position.
  • enforcement: full provenance timeline, registry hits, current location, holder pseudonym, and contact escrow
    Reason: Source communities have a legitimate interest in cultural claim information but not in institutional or enforcement internals. The orthogonal role model prevents this role from seeing museum or enforcement data regardless of ladder position.
  • owner: holder identity and all fields above
    Reason: Source communities have a legitimate interest in cultural claim information but not in institutional or enforcement internals. The orthogonal role model prevents this role from seeing museum or enforcement data regardless of ladder position.

Description: An accredited cultural institution. Sees curatorial and condition detail needed to assess a loan or an acquisition.

Fields visible:
  • public: object identity, title, artist, cultural context, image hash, confidence score, coverage class, and the notarisation proof
  • museum: physical dimensions, condition, loan eligibility, risk flags, and forensic scores

Fields withheld:
  • source-community: claim status, custodianship terms, and source-community statements
    Reason: Community-facing fields (claim status, custodianship) are tagged source-community and are not visible to ladder roles. They belong to the community, not the institution.
  • enforcement: full provenance timeline, registry hits, current location, holder pseudonym, and contact escrow
    Reason: Requires "enforcement" access level; this role is at "museum" on the disclosure ladder.
  • owner: holder identity and all fields above
    Reason: Requires "owner" access level; this role is at "museum" on the disclosure ladder.
disclosure.enforcement:
Role: Enforcement
Description: Carabinieri TPC, INTERPOL, or an equivalent authority. Sees the full provenance narrative, register hits and the escrowed contact route to the holder.

Fields visible:
  • public: object identity, title, artist, cultural context, image hash, confidence score, coverage class, and the notarisation proof
  • museum: physical dimensions, condition, loan eligibility, risk flags, and forensic scores
  • enforcement: full provenance timeline, registry hits, current location, holder pseudonym, and contact escrow

Fields withheld:
  • source-community: claim status, custodianship terms, and source-community statements
    Reason: Community-facing fields (claim status, custodianship) are tagged source-community and are not visible to ladder roles. They belong to the community, not the institution.
  • owner: holder identity and all fields above
    Reason: Requires "owner" access level; this role is at "enforcement" on the disclosure ladder.
disclosure.owner:
Role: Owner
Description: The holder of the object, identified only by a pseudonymous key. Sees everything, because it is their own record.

Fields visible:
  • public: object identity, title, artist, cultural context, image hash, confidence score, coverage class, and the notarisation proof
  • source-community: claim status, custodianship terms, and source-community statements
  • museum: physical dimensions, condition, loan eligibility, risk flags, and forensic scores
  • enforcement: full provenance timeline, registry hits, current location, holder pseudonym, and contact escrow
  • owner: holder identity and all fields above

Fields withheld:
  (none — this role sees everything)
